documents.title: H&P - Admission, ED to Medicine
lines: CHIEF COMPLAINT:
Confusion and fever brought in by daughter.
HPI:
77 yo female brought to ED at 02:10 for 1 day of confusion, decreased oral intake, and urinary frequency with dysuria for 3 days.
[GCS] Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
Daughter states pt lives alone, manages own meds, drives locally. No prior episodes of delirium.
No cough, no chest pain, no abdominal pain reported, no diarrhea. No falls witnessed.
Had 2 days of chills at home, took acetaminophen last night without relief.
TRIAGE VITALS (02:10):
[WBC] Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
[respiratory rate] Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
PMH:
Hypertension. Type 2 diabetes, diet controlled. Osteoarthritis. Recurrent UTI x2 in past year. Prior cholecystectomy.
HOME MEDS:
Amlodipine 5 mg daily.
Lisinopril 10 mg daily.
Atorvastatin 20 mg nightly.
Acetaminophen 500 mg prn.
ALLERGIES: sulfa - rash.
SOCIAL: lives alone in single-level home, daughter checks daily. Nonsmoker, no alcohol.
FAMILY HX: noncontributory.
ROS: positive for fever, chills, dysuria, weakness. Negative for vomiting, hematuria, rash, neck stiffness.
EXAM:
Gen: ill appearing elderly female, warm, dry mucous membranes.
HEENT: no scleral icterus, oropharynx dry.
Neck: supple, no JVD.
Cardiac: tachycardic, regular, no murmur.
Chest: clear to auscultation bilaterally, no crackles or wheeze, breathing unlabored.
Abd: soft, mild suprapubic tenderness, no guarding, no CVA tenderness.
Ext: warm, no edema, cap refill 3 sec at fingertips.
Skin: no rash, no cellulitis, no decubitus.
Neuro: arousable, follows simple commands, oriented to self only, no focal deficit, no asterixis.
ED COURSE:
[bolus] Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77.

[culture] Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
[antibiotic] Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
LABS:
[creatinine] Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Na 133, K 4.2, CO2 20, BUN 38, glucose 168.
Total bili 0.9, AST 28, ALT 22, alk phos 88.
CXR: no infiltrate, no effusion.
ASSESSMENT:
77 yo female with sepsis, most likely urinary source, with acute delirium, AKI, and thrombocytopenia.
Hypotension responsive to volume; no vasopressor required at this time.
PLAN:
1. Sepsis/urosepsis - continue IV antibiotics, narrow when cultures return.
2. Cultures as above, follow speciation and sensitivities.
3. AKI - hold lisinopril, hold amlodipine while soft pressures, avoid nephrotoxins, maintenance normal saline at 100 mL/hr, strict I/O, daily BMP.
4. Thrombocytopenia - trend CBC daily, no anticoagulation for now, SCDs for VTE prophylaxis.
5. Delirium - orientation cues, sitter if needed, avoid benzodiazepines and anticholinergics, sleep hygiene.
6. Foley not placed; bladder scan prn for retention.
7. Diet: carb modified, assist with PO intake; glucose checks q6h.
8. Telemetry, admit to stepdown.
9. Updated daughter at bedside 03:40, agrees with plan. Full code confirmed.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD2 Morning
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt more awake this AM, took 2 sips of broth overnight. Reports dysuria improved. Still intermittently confused at 04:00 per RN, calmer by 06:30.
Afebrile since 22:00. Urine output 620 mL over 12 hours.
Daughter at bedside, states pt recognizes her and is closer to baseline than yesterday.
OBJECTIVE:
Tmax 37.8 C overnight. BP 108/66 at 06:00.
Gen: less ill appearing, mucous membranes moist.
Cardiac: regular rate, no murmur. Chest: clear bilaterally.
Abd: soft, minimal suprapubic tenderness. Ext: no edema.
Neuro: oriented to self and place, knows she is in hospital, follows commands, no focal deficit.
LABS HD2:
WBC 16,400. Platelets 91,000. Creatinine 2.1 mg/dL. K 4.0, CO2 22, BUN 34.
Urine culture pending. Blood cultures with no growth reported as of 06:00.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
Sepsis, urinary source - clinically improving. Continue piperacillin-tazobactam and vancomycin pending speciation.
AKI - creatinine trending down with volume. Continue normal saline at 75 mL/hr, reassess at noon. Lisinopril remains on hold.
Thrombocytopenia - platelets rising, likely sepsis related. Recheck CBC in AM.
Delirium - improving, continue nonpharmacologic measures, no restraints needed.
Mobility - PT consult for gait assessment, up to chair with 1 assist today.
Diet advanced to soft, encourage PO fluids, continue strict I/O.
SCDs continued for VTE prophylaxis.
Discussed trajectory with daughter at 08:15.

documents.title: Progress Note - HD4
lines: SUBJECTIVE:
Pt alert, conversational, oriented to self, place, time, and situation. Ate 80% of breakfast. No dysuria. Ambulated 60 feet in hallway with walker and 1 assist.
No fever since HD2. Denies chest pain, dyspnea, or dizziness on standing.
OBJECTIVE:
Afebrile. BP 124/72 seated at 07:30, no orthostatic symptoms reported.
Gen: comfortable, sitting in chair.
Cardiac: regular, no murmur. Chest: clear, no accessory muscle use.
Abd: soft, nontender. Ext: trace bilateral ankle edema, new since fluids.
Neuro: back to baseline mentation per daughter.
MICRO/LABS:
Blood culture grew E. coli, sensitive to ceftriaxone and to ciprofloxacin. Urine culture with same organism, greater than 100,000 CFU/mL.
Vancomycin discontinued yesterday evening; IV antibiotics completed through day 3, now transitioned to oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID.
WBC 9,800. Platelets 148,000. Creatinine 1.2 mg/dL. Na 137, K 4.1, CO2 24, BUN 20.
ASSESSMENT/PLAN:
1. E. coli bacteremia with urosepsis - defervesced, leukocytosis resolving. Continue oral therapy, total 10 day course planned. Repeat blood culture drawn HD3 pending.
2. AKI - near baseline. IV fluids stopped at 08:00, encourage PO intake, recheck BMP in AM.
3. Thrombocytopenia - resolved.
4. Hypertension - restart amlodipine 5 mg today; hold lisinopril until outpatient recheck of renal function.
5. Delirium - resolved, no sitter.
6. PT recommends home with daughter checking daily; no SNF needed.
7. Anticipate discharge tomorrow if BMP stable and remains afebrile.

documents.title: Discharge Summary - HD5
lines: ADMITTING DIAGNOSIS: Sepsis, suspected urinary source.
DISCHARGE DIAGNOSES:
1. Sepsis secondary to E. coli urinary tract infection with bacteremia.
2. Acute kidney injury, resolved.
3. Thrombocytopenia, resolved.
4. Acute delirium, resolved.
5. Hypertension.
6. Type 2 diabetes, diet controlled.
HOSPITAL COURSE:
77 yo female presented at 02:10 with fever and confusion.
[GCS] Daughter reports patient normally independent and oriented; on arrival confused, oriented to self only, GCS 13.
[WBC] Temperature 39.4 C at triage; WBC 21,300 with 14% bands.
[respiratory rate] Respiratory rate 22; SpO2 95% on RA, no oxygen needed.
[bolus] Received 1 L normal saline bolus; BP after bolus 102/64, MAP 77. No vasopressors required at any point.

[culture] Urinalysis with large leukocyte esterase and more than 50 WBC per high power field; blood culture x2 and urine culture drawn at 02:20 before antibiotics; blood culture positive for E. coli at 30 hours.
[antibiotic] Piperacillin-tazobactam 4.5 g IV given at 02:45, 35 minutes after arrival; vancomycin added; remained on IV antibiotics through day 3.
[creatinine] Creatinine 2.6 mg/dL (baseline 0.9 mg/dL); platelets 84,000.
Renal function improved with volume resuscitation: creatinine 2.1 on HD2, 1.2 on HD4, 1.0 on HD5. Platelets 148,000 on HD4.
Vancomycin stopped HD3 after speciation. Narrowed to oral ciprofloxacin 500 mg BID on HD4 per sensitivities.
Repeat blood culture drawn HD3 showed no growth. Afebrile since HD2. Mentation returned to baseline by HD4 per daughter.
PT evaluated and cleared for home with walker; ambulated 60 feet with 1 assist.
CONDITION AT DISCHARGE: stable, afebrile, ambulatory with walker, at baseline mentation.
DISCHARGE MEDICATIONS:
Ciprofloxacin 500 mg PO BID to complete 10 day total course - 5 days remaining.
Amlodipine 5 mg PO daily.
Atorvastatin 20 mg PO nightly.
Acetaminophen 500 mg PO q6h prn.
Lisinopril HELD - do not resume until renal function rechecked by primary clinician.
FOLLOW-UP:
Primary care in 5 to 7 days for BMP and blood pressure check.
Urology referral placed for recurrent UTI evaluation.
DISCHARGE INSTRUCTIONS:
Drink at least 6 to 8 glasses of water daily. Complete all antibiotic doses.
Return for fever above 38.0 C, new confusion, decreased urination, back pain, or vomiting.
Daughter to stay with pt for first 48 hours and assist with medications. Instructions reviewed with pt and daughter at 11:20; both verbalized understanding.
